publicationStmt.p: Amores Project transcription, 9 September 2026. Two source readings completed; human scholarly approval is not implied.

handDesc.handNote: The main verse text is written in brown ink. Layout, visible signs and annotations are transcribed without assigning historical hands from colour alone. Long s and ordinary letter allographs are represented by standard Latin characters.

origin.p: The source manifest dates this composite manuscript to the 11th and 12th centuries. The catalogue date is not a date for every intervention.

surrogates.p: Actual source pages 388, 389 were inspected at full resolution and in enlarged crops. Viewer page numbers are one-based indices into the manifest, not manuscript page labels. e-codices IIIF source manifest

projectDesc.p: All 48 extant verse positions were read directly from source images by the first reader and independently by a different agent. Original annotation rectangles are preserved. No other witness supplied readings. Word spacing and couplet grouping are editorial.

correction.p: Visible letters are retained even where they differ from familiar readings. Tentative paleography is localized with unclear. A missing written initial is represented as gap, without inventing its decoration. Marginal annotations are not silently substituted into the verse. Ink colour alone does not establish an erased reading or historical hand.

normalization.p: u/v and e caudata follow visible source forms as far as practicable. Long s and ordinary letter allographs use standard characters. Combining macrons represent visible suspension/contraction bars schematically. Abbreviations are paired with defensible expansions in choice/abbr/expan; unexplained letters are not expanded merely to match a familiar edition. Special glyph approximations are declared in charDecl. Their form is typographic rather than a facsimile drawing.

punctuation.p: Visible stops are transcribed as schematic dots or colons. Modern punctuation is not supplied. Word spaces are editorial except where space explicitly records a significant physical separation.

segmentation.p: Every verse has a stable ID and a facs pointer to a rectangle on the correct manifest canvas. Annotation page values are interpreted through the manifest index. Physical page changes are pb elements within logical couplets where necessary. Source text beyond the poem is used to verify boundaries but not included as verse.
Full-page source inspection shows aligned regular verse initials, without systematic alternate-line indentation. The explicit space and smaller writing at the opening remain separate.

interpretation.p: Every first-reader note was investigated during an independent all-line source review. Supported corrections are incorporated and local uncertainty is documented without becoming an automatic user task. Note dispositions and actual page coverage are recorded in the review ledger.

div.head: Reviewed transcription notes
div.note: The separate E, broad space and smaller writing of the opening are visible on page 388. The short group after deos remains tentatively ine: its joined strokes do not securely distinguish an alternative reading. The right inscription ad p̄iurā amicā is retained with conventional expansions. The layout and writing size do not identify a historical hand.
The independent source reading confirms the bars in Quā and n̄dū, represented schematically and expanded Quam and nondum. The remaining words and terminal stop agree with the image.

The horizontal cancellation through the short barred group before numina is visible. Its tentative letters nū remain unclear inside del; no complete earlier word or sequence of historical hands is inferred. The following numina lesit habet is retained.
Both occurrences of longa decensqꝫ and the final manet are visible. The repeated wording and que suspensions are retained as written.

The enlarged verb has a crowded sequence of low strokes between radi- and the final t. The tentative radiauit is retained under unclear; the image does not securely separate every minim or establish an alternative ending.

The contraction after Scilicet has a visible bar and joined minims. Its schematic source form ōne is retained, with omne explicitly a qualified expansion. The following falsū and iurare puellis are supported.
The crossed-p sign followed by q and a que suspension is visible. The following suos illā nuper iurasse recordor agrees with the source, including the contracted illā.

The marked group after At has merged strokes and a bar. The tentative cūs is now explicitly an unclear abbreviation and remains unexpanded. Meriti cur ego damna tuli is retained without grammatical emendation.
The source supports inuidię with a descending caudata, the suspension uobꝰ, the spelling cepheia and the final est contraction. No spelling is normalized.
The enlarged initial sign has the looped p form represented by the declared pro glyph. Male formosa iussa parente mori is visible; the glyph does not assert an addition or a correction.

The enlarged opening supports Non satis, correcting first-pass Non sitis. The following marked e remains an unexpanded abbreviation. The later siue/sine distinction remains locally unclear; the physical blemish beside testes is not treated as an erasure.
The source supports Et mecū, followed by a crowded word tentatively lusos and then irride multa deos. The uncertain internal letter shapes are retained locally; word order is not emended.

The first marked word after sua contains more strokes than the first-pass p̄iuri. The crossed-p is followed by a tentative iurān sequence with a visible bar; this remains unexpanded and unclear. The final faded p̄tis is also an unclear abbreviation. No complete reading is imported to resolve either contraction.

Page 389 begins with this verse. Virgine, decepta and deceptore are pale and remain locally unclear; the mark near the end of decepta cannot be securely separated from surrounding ascenders as an independent abbreviation mark. Final suo is visible. Fading does not establish missing transmission.

The faint middle groups remain tentatively per nōn under unclear. The following d̄s and ē are explicitly retained as unexpanded abbreviations. Final feminaqꝫ tantū is supported; no syntax-driven reconstruction is supplied.
The short group between forma and credulitate looks ppos and remains an unclear, unexpanded abbreviation. The surrounding words and initial et ligature are supported by the image.
At tu sis and ceteras amat ille puellas remain the source reading. The intervening marked d̄s and ē are explicit unexpanded abbreviations; their intended construction is not silently supplied.

The verb ends in a marked t. The source form accingit̄ is now retained instead of writing accingit as an unmarked full word; accingitur is a qualified expansion. Nobꝰ fatifero mauors and ense remain supported.
The source has curuant̄ with a final suspension, corrected from the fully written-out first-pass curuantur. Nobis flexibiles, apollinis and arcꝰ are retained; curuantur is available as the expansion.
Visible marks contract the word after metuunt. The schematic offēdē is now displayed, with offendere as a qualified expansion. Formosas superi metuunt and lesi remain supported by the source.
The faded word after pia uiolat remains tentatively focis. The marked q̄sqꝫ and inpūe are supported. No competing construction or reading is supplied to resolve the uncertain word.
The short form before uiris has a mark over its later letters; the first-pass additional bar over the initial i was not supported. It is represented inē, with inesse a qualified expansion.
The ornate initial M and following issaqꝫ are visible. Periuras tela ferire uetat agrees with the image; the initial is not interpreted as an et ligature or a cancellation.
The source contracts mat̄s as well as pat̄ and opꝰ. The missed matris contraction is now explicit. The spelling bacho and the surrounding words remain unchanged.
Both parallel clauses use q̄qꝫ and h̄nt; oculos and pectꝰ are visible. Each written contraction is retained alongside its expansion.

The source opening is Si d̄s ipse foret. The marked group before sine is shorter than a fully written numen and is retained tentatively as nūn, unexpanded and unclear. The following sine fraude liceret is supported.
The source displays a contraction bar in mēdaci. The full mendaci of the first pass has been moved to the expansion; Femina, falleret ore and meū remain supported.

The final bar of iurarē is visible in the enlargement. The first-pass unmarked, unclear iurare has been replaced by the written abbreviation, with iurarem as a qualified expansion. The following uerū iurasse puellas remains supported.

The n̄ suspension is retained, with non as a qualified expansion instead of the unsupported nam. After diceret the marked e/t-like group is longer than the first-pass ē and remains tentatively eēt, unexpanded and unclear. Final d̄s is retained.

The final suspended word has a possible baseline minim before the raised ending sign. It is represented moderat[i]ꝰ with the i locally unclear, and moderatius explicitly a low-certainty expansion. The preceding t̄m and illor̄ remain written contractions; no missing ending is asserted as certain.
Aut oculis certe parce puella meis and its terminal stop are visible. The following poem opens below this verse and is used only as boundary evidence.
